client: BAE Systems Pension Scheme and BAE Systems Executive Pension Scheme
date: 2023-09-06 (announced); transition expected towards end of 2023; scheme SIPs updated 11 July 2024
strategy: Outsourced chief investment officer for the schemes' DB assets, including liability-driven and cashflow-driven portfolios; in-house investment team (BAE Systems Pension Funds Investment Management) moved to GSAM and continues to serve the schemes
amount_basis: UK defined benefit scheme assets handed over for management at announcement. Not a fee figure and not a statement of fee-paying AUM by strategy.
rationale: Sponsor: 'reducing the cost and improving the efficiency of asset management are essential'. Trustee chair credited the in-house team's stewardship and framed the move as a long-term solution. Selected after a 'highly competitive tender process'.
consultant: Redington (trustees' strategic investment adviser since 2021; advised on the deal and oversees implementation). Travers Smith (trustees' lawyers). PwC advised the sponsor. Gallagher is named as the trustee's investment adviser in the 2026 implementation statement.
decision_makers: Trustees of both schemes (chair Andrew Gallagher); sponsor group finance director Brad Greve quoted
gs_team_attribution: Press release quotes Ed Francis as Head of International OCIO and UK Fiduciary Management, with David Solomon and Marc Nachmann. No source attributes the win to a sales or coverage team or to any other individual.
notes: Described by Goldman as the largest OCIO mandate awarded in the UK to that date. Still in force: the scheme's implementation statement for the year to 31 March 2026 calls GSAM 'the Scheme's OCIO'. The trustee retains a separate investment adviser, so OCIO did not remove independent oversight. Number of staff transferred is not public.

client: Various pension entities and a captive insurance company related to Shell plc (UK, Germany, Bermuda and other locations); advisory for North American plans
client_type: Corporate pension funds and captive insurer
country: United Kingdom / Germany / other Europe / North America (advisory)
date: 2025-09-09 (announced); transitions expected to complete later in 2025
strategy: OCIO for international pension plan assets in Europe (includes LDI and CDI); investment advisory services for North American plans
amount: $40 billion in total; of which about $15.6 billion (about £11.5bn) UK and $2.8 billion Germany
amount_basis: Pension plan and captive assets covered by the mandates at announcement. The rest of the $40bn is not itemised. No asset figure is given for the North American advisory element. Not fee-paying AUM by strategy.
rationale: Marc Nachmann: asset owners 'increasingly want differentiated alpha, holistic total portfolio advice and customized portfolio solutions'. Each fund 'set clear objectives and selection criteria'. Shell spokesperson: Shell acted as coordinator; decisions were made by the individual funds.
decision_makers: Trustees of each fund, deciding separately
gs_team_attribution: Press release quotes Chloe Kipling, co-head of EMEA Institutional Client Coverage, and Marc Nachmann. mallowstreet reports 'some staff will move to GSAM'. No further team attribution is public.
notes: The Dutch Shell fund (SSPF) is not part of this: it appointed BlackRock in 2024. That shows one sponsor's schemes can choose different OCIO providers. Completion of the transition has not been separately confirmed in a source read for this register.

client: Two UK pension schemes within the Short Brothers Common Investment Fund
strategy: Fiduciary management: diversified strategy with bespoke hedging, investing across asset classes through internal and external managers
amount_basis: Combined assets of the two schemes at announcement
rationale: Common Investment Fund chair Ken Brundle: 'Following a rigorous process, we concluded that Goldman Sachs Asset Management offered a solution' suited to the fund's objectives.
decision_makers: Trustees of the Common Investment Fund (chair Ken Brundle)
gs_team_attribution: Ed Francis quoted as managing director and head of UK fiduciary management. No other attribution.
notes: Source labels this 'fiduciary management', the usual UK term; 'OCIO' is used for the larger later deals. The page date reads '10/5/22', taken as 10 May 2022.

client: Calor Group Retirement Benefits Plan (trustee: Calor Pension Trust)
strategy: Fiduciary management of the plan's DB assets, replacing Cardano
amount_basis: Plan assets at the time of reporting
rationale: Publicly stated only that the appointment followed a competitive tender; reported as part of a trend of schemes reviewing existing fiduciary arrangements
notes: A replacement win: the plan had been under fiduciary management since 2019 and its statement for the year to 5 April 2024 names Cardano as fiduciary manager. Shows fiduciary mandates are re-tendered and can be lost by the incumbent.

date: After 31 March 2025; exact date not public (announced in the scheme's 2026 member newsletter)
strategy: Fiduciary management; trustees say they are working with GSAM to review the investment mix
amount_basis: Not disclosed. The scheme as a whole was valued at £645.5m at 31 March 2025; the newsletter does not say how much GSAM manages.
rationale: Trustees: since 31 March 2025 they have been 'working to ensure the Scheme is better placed for the years ahead'
notes: Found only in the scheme's own member communication, not in trade press. Previous fiduciary manager, tender process and adviser are not stated in the page read.

strategy: Fiduciary management, replacing Mercer
amount_basis: Mandate size as reported
rationale: Not visible (article paywalled)
notes: Reported as the first UK fiduciary appointment GSAM had publicly announced. Useful as the starting point of the UK fiduciary business that later won BAE.

client: UPS (United Parcel Service) US and Canadian defined benefit pension plans
date: 2024-05-16 (announced); investment team joined GSAM on 1 September 2024
strategy: OCIO for DB plan assets; UPS's in-house investment staff (22 people including the CIO) joined GSAM in Atlanta
amount_basis: Plan assets as of 31 March 2024. P&I later cites $41.5bn overseen by the CIO before the move.
rationale: UPS said benefits and plan administration would not change. P&I: GSAM's model is to take the whole team so 'the transition is likely to be much smoother'.
consultant: A third-party consultant led the search according to Goldman (consultant not named in sources read)
gs_team_attribution: P&I quotes Christopher Keogh (global co-head, institutional client business), Timothy Braude and Alexandra Wilson-Elizondo (multi-asset solutions) and Gregory Calnon. These are US/global roles; nothing links the deal to London.
notes: Non-EMEA but the clearest public description of how an OCIO liftout works in practice and what happens to the client's staff.

client_type: Corporate DB and DC retirement plans
strategy: OCIO for DB plans of both companies; advisory for Verizon's DC assets
amount: Over $70 billion: $30 billion DB OCIO assets under management (both companies) and $40 billion DC assets under advisement (Verizon)
amount_basis: The release itself separates assets under management from assets under advisement. Advisory assets normally earn a different, usually lower, fee than managed assets; no fees are disclosed.
rationale: Marc Nachmann: the mandates 'affirm our ability to deliver customised public and private market investment solutions'
gs_team_attribution: Only Marc Nachmann quoted. US mandates.
notes: Non-EMEA. Included because it is the most recent large OCIO win before the cutoff and because the AUM versus AUA split is a good teaching example. OCIO AUS reported as $480bn as of 31 March 2026.

country: Canada / United Kingdom (not specified in source)
strategy: Pension and insurance mandate with members of Bombardier's in-house investment team joining Goldman
amount_basis: As reported by Institutional Investor; basis not specified
notes: Known here only from one trade article's retrospective paragraph. The primary announcement was not located (search budget ran out), so details such as which plans and whether UK schemes were included are not established.

client: Pacific Global Advisors (2015), Verus OCIO business (2017), Aptitude Investment Management (2018)
strategy: Acquisitions that built GSAM's OCIO scale: Pacific Global Advisors ($18bn, large pension plans), Verus's OCIO business ($21bn), Aptitude (hedge fund solutions; formerly Weyerhaeuser's in-house pension team)
amount: $18 billion and $21 billion for the first two
amount_basis: Assets of the acquired businesses as reported
notes: Context: part of GSAM's OCIO assets were bought or lifted out, not won mandate by mandate. Relevant when reading growth figures.

client: NN Group (acquisition of NN Investment Partners and long-term asset management partnership)
strategy: Purchase of NN Investment Partners; reported ten-year strategic partnership under which GSAM manages NN Group's insurance portfolio
amount: €1.7 billion purchase price; partnership portfolio reported as about $190 billion (2021 coverage) and about $180 billion (later coverage)
amount_basis: Price paid for the business. The partnership figure is the insurer's portfolio to be managed, as reported by secondary sources; the primary release could not be fetched.
rationale: Reported aim: expand GSAM's European presence; NN Group to concentrate on insurance
gs_team_attribution: David Solomon quoted at completion. More than 900 NN IP employees joined; the Netherlands became a significant GSAM location.
notes: Purchase price, staff numbers and the rise of GSAM's European AUS to more than $600bn are verified from fetched trade sources. The ten-year term and portfolio size rest on search-result passages from secondary sources, and two figures circulate ($190bn and $180bn), probably from different dates. This is a large insurance mandate acquired through M&A, not a sales win.

strategy: Separately managed account co-investing in private credit across Asia Pacific, with a focus on India; managed by Private Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives
amount_basis: Size of the separately managed account to be deployed over time ('long-term capital'), not drawn or fee-paying capital at signing
rationale: Mubadala building Asia Pacific private debt exposure; Goldman expanding its Asia credit platform
decision_makers: Mubadala (Omar Eraiqat, Deputy CEO of Diversified Investments; Fabrizio Bocciardi, Head of Credit Investments)
gs_team_attribution: Managed by Private Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives; Marc Nachmann and Greg Olafson quoted. No client coverage team is named.
notes: The release also recalls Goldman's 2023 decision to open an office in Abu Dhabi Global Market. An example of a sovereign relationship structured as a bespoke account, not a fund subscription.

strategy: Non-binding MoU: PIF to act as strategic anchor investor for new GSAM private credit and public equity strategies focused on Saudi Arabia and the GCC
amount_basis: No amount disclosed
rationale: PIF developing local asset management and attracting international capital; Goldman expanding in Riyadh
decision_makers: PIF (Yazeed A. Al-Humied, Deputy Governor and Head of MENA Investments)
gs_team_attribution: Marc Nachmann named. No coverage team named.
notes: An MoU is an intention, not a funded mandate. Subject to regulatory and internal approvals. No launched fund or close was found before the cutoff.

strategy: MoU to expand an existing partnership: QIA to target combined commitments to GSAM-managed funds and co-investments and act as anchor investor in several strategies; Goldman to grow Doha into its largest regional asset management office
amount_basis: A target for combined future commitments under an MoU that 'remains subject to certain terms, conditions and deliverables'. Not committed, drawn or fee-paying capital.
rationale: QIA CEO: the commitment 'will deliver meaningful benefits to our economy'
decision_makers: QIA (CEO Mohammed Saif Al Sowaidi); Goldman Sachs (David Solomon)
notes: Conflicting wording between sources: the joint statement says 'target'; Institutional Investor's headline says 'Commits $25B'. Treat it as a target. Focus areas reported as AI, fintech, digital infrastructure and private credit.

strategy: Strategic collaboration to deliver public and private market solutions for retirement and wealth investors; Goldman to buy T. Rowe Price shares
amount: Up to $1 billion of T. Rowe Price stock (intention to own up to 3.5%)
amount_basis: Equity investment by Goldman, not client assets. The 'up to 3.5%' and product timing come from sources not fetched.
rationale: Combine T. Rowe's retirement franchise with Goldman's private markets capabilities
notes: The $1bn position and the 'strategic collaboration' are confirmed in a fetched article; the stake ceiling, co-branded target-date products and mid-2026 launch timing are from search-result passages only. US-focused, but relevant to how GSAM reaches retirement and wealth channels through partners.

strategy: Acquisition of a defined-outcome ETF provider
amount: About $31 billion of AUS acquired; price reported as about $2 billion
amount_basis: AUS is Innovator's fee-based discretionary client assets as of 28 February 2026. The price is from Reuters via a search-result passage; Goldman's completion release gives no price.
rationale: Expand GSAM's active ETF business: about 240 ETFs and about $90bn ETF AUS pro forma
gs_team_attribution: More than 70 Innovator employees joined; two executives joined as partners.
notes: Shows growth in the third-party wealth and ETF channel through acquisition. Price is Supported inference only.

client: European investors (UCITS active fixed income ETFs)
client_type: Product launch for wealth and institutional channels
strategy: First active ETFs in Europe: USD and EUR investment-grade corporate bond active UCITS ETFs
amount_basis: No assets disclosed. Reported total expense ratio 0.25% (a published fund charge)
notes: Launch details come from a search-result summary of an article that could not be fetched; the April 2025 Goldman release confirms that active fixed income ETFs had already been launched in EMEA. A product launch is not a mandate and carries no client assets by itself.

client_type: Product launch for wealth and institutional channels
country: Europe (listed in London and Frankfurt, further listings planned)
strategy: Goldman Sachs Alpha Enhanced US Equity Active UCITS ETF (GQUS), first of five active equity ETFs (US, global, European, Japanese, emerging markets), run by Quantitative Investment Strategies
amount_basis: No assets disclosed at launch
rationale: Hilary Lopez described the earlier fixed income funds as core active building blocks and the equity range as the next step
gs_team_attribution: Hilary Lopez quoted as Head of the EMEA Third Party Wealth Business; Hania Schmidt as Head of Quantitative Investment Strategies in EMEA.
notes: One of the few public documents that names the EMEA Third Party Wealth business and its head in connection with a product.

client: High-net-worth investors in Europe (first private markets ELTIF)
client_type: Product launch / fund close for wealth channel
strategy: First private markets European Long-Term Investment Fund, closed-end; reported as mostly private equity with some private credit
amount_basis: Capital raised at the fund's close. Closed-end structure with a lock-up of up to nine years per secondary reporting.
notes: Amount and investor type verified from the fetched (paywalled) article; strategy mix and lock-up from search-result passages. Small beside institutional mandates: wealth-channel private markets products raise money in many small tickets through intermediaries.

client: Eligible investors in certain European jurisdictions (G-European Credit ELTIF; G-Series evergreen funds)
strategy: First evergreen product under ELTIF 2.0, extending an evergreen European private credit strategy launched in October 2023; joins a G-Series of six evergreen private markets funds
amount: Existing European private credit evergreen strategy: over $8 billion including leverage
amount_basis: As of 4 March 2026: fair value of private and liquid credit investments plus unfunded commitments, including leverage, excluding cash. It is not investor net assets and not the new ELTIF's size.
rationale: Give a wider range of investors access to private markets
gs_team_attribution: Stephanie Rader (Global Co-Head of Alternatives Capital Formation) and James Reynolds (Global Co-Head of Private Credit) quoted.
notes: A good example for checking a headline number: '$8bn' includes leverage and unfunded commitments.

client: Border to Coast Pensions Partnership (Emerging Markets Equity Alpha Fund)
strategy: Emerging markets ex-China equity sleeve, alongside Baillie Gifford; UBS and FountainCap appointed for China
amount: Sleeve about two-thirds of a roughly £700 million fund, shared between two managers
amount_basis: Size of the pool's new fund at launch, not GSAM's allocation, which is not disclosed
decision_makers: Border to Coast (pool operator), on behalf of partner funds
notes: The 2023 appointment details are from search-result passages (IPE could not be fetched). A fetched 2025 article confirms Goldman Sachs was managing the pool's emerging markets allocation in March 2025. Example of selling to an LGPS pool, not to individual funds.

amount_basis: Not disclosed

strategy: UK and overseas equities mandate ended
amount_basis: Mandate size as reported
rationale: Strategic asset allocation reshuffle
notes: Old, but shows a mandate lost because the client changed strategy, not because of a stated failing.

strategy: Recommendation to end the fund's fixed income mandates with Goldman Sachs, Schroders and CQS
amount_basis: Not established
rationale: Not read; the paper could not be fetched
decision_makers: Kent Pension Fund Committee / Pension Board
notes: Known only from a search-result summary of the council paper (the site returned HTTP 403). A recommendation is not a completed termination. Plausibly linked to LGPS pooling, but that is not confirmed. Needs checking against the committee minutes.

strategy: Fiduciary management of all the fund's assets (equities, fixed income, hedge funds)
amount_basis: Fund assets covered at appointment
gs_team_attribution: Reported as handled by the Global Manager Strategies team led by Doug Kramer (2006).

notes: The clearest public case of a whole-portfolio mandate lost on performance. Later reporting also cited Dutch regulatory change and distance of a US firm; that is from a search-result passage only.

strategy: Global quantitative equity
amount_basis: Mandate size as reported

strategy: Specialist European equities
amount_basis: Mandate size as reported

client: True Potential Investments (True Potential Wealth Platform)
strategy: Exclusive distribution of Goldman Sachs multi-asset dynamic strategy funds to UK retail investors through over 800 adviser firms

notes: Historical example of the intermediary chain: the platform decides what advisers can access; underlying investors are the advisers' clients. Whether the arrangement still exists was not checked.

client: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (regulatory action against Goldman Sachs Asset Management, L.P.)
strategy: Policies and procedures failures for two mutual funds and one separately managed account strategy marketed as ESG investments (April 2017 to February 2020)
amount_basis: Civil penalty
rationale: SEC: no written ESG research policies for one product until June 2018, then not followed consistently until February 2020
notes: 'Regulatory action' is added to the kind vocabulary so that the register is not only wins. GSAM neither admitted nor denied the findings. Relevant to client due diligence: policies were shared with intermediaries and a fund board.

client: Los Angeles County Employees Retirement Association (LACERA)
strategy: Core-plus fixed income mandate terminated
amount_basis: Mandate size as reported
rationale: 'terminated to bring the core-plus exposure in line with the fund's fixed-income suballocation targets'
notes: Non-EMEA, old. Kept as a second example of a loss driven by the client's asset allocation.
